text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَرْفَعُوٓا۟ أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِىِّ وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا۟ لَهُۥ بِٱلْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ

words.gloss_range: vocative summons opening the direct address and governing the following command sequence
words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens the ayah as direct summons, so the two prohibitions are heard as addressed speech rather than detached rules. The call scopes over the whole command sequence, re-summons the believer community after 49:1, and makes hearing itself part of the scene before voices are restrained. Its long open sound also creates an audible moment of attention before the dense sequence begins.

topics.headline: vocative governs the command frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibitions arrive inside a live summons, not as impersonal etiquette rules.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the word as the opening vocative particle for the believer-address sequence.

topics.headline: summons makes hearing thematic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah first turns the addressees into hearers before correcting their own sound.
topics.reason: The sound and attention rows cohere with the local speech-and-voice setting and are not contradicted by the vocative parse.

words.gloss_range: vocative selector with alerting force, preparing the specified addressee class
words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ʾayyuhā}}) both selects and alerts the addressees. The form does not complete the audience by itself; it opens a slot that the following relative clause fills, so identity is delayed until the faith-description arrives. That alerting force matters because the ayah later warns that the same addressees may fail to perceive the consequence.

topics.headline: selection joined to alerting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the address is not merely naming a group; it selects them and wakes them to receive a warning.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the form as the called expression introduced by the vocative, and the critical rows explain its selector-alert shape.

topics.headline: identity waits for the relative clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a one-word delay before the audience is defined by faith.
topics.reason: The appositive relative attachment licenses the incomplete vocative slot that is completed by the next words.

words.gloss_range: definite plural relative pronoun that restricts the called audience by the following faith clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) restricts the summons to the ones characterized by the following faith verb. The audience is therefore not an undefined crowd; it is grammatically defined before the prohibitions begin. The familiar believer-address formula remains active, but here its payoff is specific: faith identity is immediately tested by acoustic discipline before the Prophet.

topics.headline: relative clause defines the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command first defines who is being addressed by faith before regulating their speech.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is appositive to the vocative expression and requires the following relative clause.

topics.headline: believer-address formula specialized
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a familiar believer-address genre is being specialized into voice discipline.
topics.reason: The formulaic address is locally present and its specialization is constrained by the following prohibitions.

words.gloss_range: perfect Form IV believer-status verb; locally an established faith identity that frames speech restraint
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, entrusted reliability, and belief; locally narrowed to established active commitment rather than simple safety alone
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) names the audience by an already established active commitment. The perfect Form IV does not invite initial belief here; it makes speech restraint a test of people already standing in a trust-and-faith field. The wider {{ar:أ م ن}} ({{tr:ʾ-m-n}}) range of safety, trust, and belief adds pressure without replacing the local sense, and the formulaic believer address links this verse to the surah’s later tests of claimed faith and deeds (49:14) and communal speech ethics (49:12).

topics.headline: faith identity precedes the prohibitions
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command tests an established believer identity rather than creating that identity.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect active Form IV verb in the relative clause before both prohibitions.

topics.headline: trust and safety field retained locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief here carries a trust-and-security field, so uncontrolled speech is a breach inside the identity named by the root.
topics.reason: V4 lacks a local root entry for this root, so the family pressure is kept as semantic background while QAC fixes the local Form IV believer-status verb.

topics.headline: faith formula enters surah speech tests
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believer formula frames later surah contrasts between claimed faith, deeds, and communal speech (49:12; 49:14).
topics.reason: The critical rows provide concrete same-surah and formulaic links; they illuminate the frame without changing the local verb sense.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle before a jussive verb, not factual negation in this position
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive here because it governs a jussive verb. It turns possible voice-raising into a direct negative command, and as the first of three same-sounding particles it starts the ayah’s descent from command to later factual non-perception.

topics.headline: first particle creates prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clause commands restraint rather than merely reporting that voices are not raised.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the particle complement relation to the jussive verb that follows.

topics.headline: first beat of the three-particle arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first audible stop that will be echoed by a second prohibition and then by factual negation.
topics.reason: The repeated particle pattern is visible in the local word sequence and culminates at the closing negation.

words.gloss_range: direct jussive prohibition of raising voices; locally acoustic elevation within a hierarchy frame
words.root_gloss_range: raising, elevation, rank, lifting, and submission-to-authority branches; locally narrowed to direct voice-raising with hierarchy pressure
words.prose: {{ar:تَرْفَعُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:tarfaʿū}}) carries the addressees inside the jussive verb form, so the summoned believers remain directly responsible for the act. The local command forbids acoustic elevation: the {{ar:ر ف ع}} ({{tr:r-f-ʿ}}) field of lifting and rank survives as vertical hierarchy, while the object and the following above-phrase narrow it to voice-raising. The sequence then tightens from being above the Prophet’s voice to the later prohibition of loud address, making 49:1’s precedence boundary audible and bodily.

topics.headline: jussive form directly restrains the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reduced jussive form directly targets the believers’ own acoustic action.
topics.reason: The verb is a second-person masculine plural jussive after prohibitive negation, with the subject carried in the morphology.

topics.headline: raising narrowed to acoustic hierarchy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that voice-raising is framed as an upward trespass in hierarchy, not just extra volume.
topics.reason: The object voices and the above phrase select the acoustic branch, while the root’s rank and elevation associations remain locally relevant as hierarchy pressure; cross-root parallels are illustrative and do not govern the parse.

topics.headline: first restraint narrows into second restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from spatial overstepping to social loudness as two coordinated speech restraints.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the later verb with this one, and the contextual rows link the acoustic scene to the preceding authority boundary in 49:1.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural voices as the object of the raising prohibition, locally controllable sound output
words.root_gloss_range: voice, sound, cry, and audible signal; locally narrowed to the believers’ produced voices rather than political or unrelated sound senses
words.prose: {{ar:أَصْوَٰتَكُمْ}} ({{tr:aṣwātakum}}) is the possessed plural object of the raising verb, so the prohibited material is the believers’ own controllable sound. The {{ar:ص و ت}} ({{tr:ṣ-w-t}}) range makes the issue broader than word-choice alone: audible emission itself is being regulated. Its plural form is measured against the singular prophetic voice, and that plural-singular echo anticipates the lowered-voice counterpart in 49:3.

topics.headline: owned voices become the controlled object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that many owned believer voices are measured against one prophetic voice.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word the accusative object of the raising verb, and the possessive suffix identifies the addressees as owners of the sound.

topics.headline: sound emission narrowed from broad root range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition reaches sound-level dominance before the content of speech is even assessed.
topics.reason: The local noun means voices in context; broader sound and modern extensions are kept only insofar as they sharpen audible emission, not as separate local senses.

topics.headline: voice root concentrates across the scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an acoustic thread from these voices to the Prophet’s singular voice and then to the lowered voices of 49:3.
topics.reason: The same-root local recurrence and the next-ayah counterpart are directly tied to the voice terminology.

words.gloss_range: spatial-above adverb used as a preposition, locally setting the Prophet’s voice as the threshold
words.root_gloss_range: aboveness, superiority, surpassing, and excess; locally narrowed to an acoustic threshold of above/over
words.prose: {{ar:فَوْقَ}} ({{tr:fawqa}}) supplies the above-relation for the first prohibition. As a spatial adverb used prepositionally, it makes the Prophet’s voice a threshold: the issue is not generic volume but being over that measure. The {{ar:ف و ق}} ({{tr:f-w-q}}) field of aboveness, surpassing, and excess survives as hierarchy pressure while the local construction keeps the sense tied to acoustic position.

topics.headline: above marks the voice threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Prophet’s voice functions as the boundary above which believers must not place their own sound.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the word an adverbial dependent of the raising verb and an idafa head governing the following voice noun.

topics.headline: surpassing field narrowed to acoustic overness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that over-volume is also overstepping, because the above-word carries superiority and excess pressure.
topics.reason: The local phrase selects spatial above, while the root range supports hierarchy and excess as controlled semantic pressure.

words.gloss_range: singular construct voice governed by above and bound to the Prophet as the measuring standard
words.root_gloss_range: voice, sound, and audible signal; locally narrowed to the singular Prophet-associated voice as measure
words.prose: {{ar:صَوْتِ}} ({{tr:ṣawti}}) is singular and in construct, first governed by the above-word and then completed by the Prophet title. That grammar makes it the calibration standard, not another owned voice among the plural voices. The repeated {{ar:ص و ت}} ({{tr:ṣ-w-t}}) root changes number and possessor, so the ayah lets the contrast between many believer voices and one prophetic voice carry the hierarchy.

topics.headline: singular construct sets the measure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one prophet-associated voice becomes the standard by which many voices are measured.
topics.reason: The word is governed by the preceding adverb and itself governs the following Prophet title in construct.

topics.headline: voice carries prophetic authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the voice is not neutral sound; it is attached to prophetic identity and to the divine-hearing frame of 49:1.
topics.reason: The construct relation and local recurrence of the sound root license the identity-bearing and acoustic-hierarchy payoff.

words.gloss_range: definite singular Prophet title in genitive construct, locally the known referent whose voice sets the measure
words.root_gloss_range: prophetic news-bearing and, in derivational dispute, elevation; locally narrowed to the known Prophet title in construct
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلنَّبِىِّ}} ({{tr:al-nabīyi}}) completes the measuring phrase as a definite, known singular title. The {{ar:ن ب أ}} ({{tr:n-b-ʾ}}) family can evoke news-bearing and, in derivational dispute, elevation, but locally the construct fixes the title as the Prophet whose voice defines the boundary. The rare pairing of Prophet-title with voice also fits the surah’s concern with reports and speech, including the later news-warning scene (49:6).

topics.headline: definite title fixes the referent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the boundary is measured by the known Prophet, not by an abstract authority figure.
topics.reason: QAC marks a definite genitive singular noun completing the construct phrase, and attachment evidence binds it to the preceding voice noun.

topics.headline: news-bearing title pressure kept local
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title carries information-authority pressure while local grammar keeps it simply the known Prophet title.
topics.reason: V4 lacks a local root entry for this root, so derivational and family pressure is retained only as title-background, not as an alternate parse.

topics.headline: Prophet title joins speech and report themes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Prophet’s voice is a rare local construction within a surah that later tests news reception (49:6).
topics.reason: The critical rows support the rare voice-title pairing and same-surah news thread without changing the local construct relation.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that joins the second prohibition to the first as an ordered follow-up
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links a second complete prohibition to the first. It does not erase the ordering: the ayah first forbids being above the Prophet’s voice, then resets with a clipped joined beat before the next loudness verb. The conjunction therefore keeps continuity and escalation together.

topics.headline: conjunction joins the second command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second prohibition is coordinated but still arrives as a fresh ordered follow-up.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the second prohibition with the first while preserving the separate following negative particle and verb.

words.gloss_range: renewed prohibitive particle before the second jussive verb, not a mere extension of the first negation
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) renews prohibition for the second speech restraint. The repeated particle makes the second command stand on its own rather than merely lengthening the first, and it sets up the later contrast with the final same-sounding particle that states non-perception instead of commanding restraint.

topics.headline: second particle restarts command force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second speech rule has its own prohibitive force while echoing the first.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the particle as governing the second jussive verb in a coordinated prohibition.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form I prohibition of overt or loud address, locally governing stacked prepositional complements
words.root_gloss_range: loudness, openness, public manifestation, and overt speech; locally narrowed to public/loud address in a prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:تَجْهَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:tajharū}}) repeats the jussive command form but shifts from vertical excess to overt loud address. The {{ar:ج ه ر}} ({{tr:j-h-r}}) range gives the verb publicity and audible emergence, while the local stacked complements specify the target, medium, and comparison. Its echo with the later loudness noun makes the second prohibition internally audible: do not address the Prophet in the kind of open peer-loudness used among yourselves.

topics.headline: second jussive targets a specified address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the loudness verb is not vague; its complements specify recipient, speech medium, and comparison.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the verb to the preceding prohibitive particle and to its following prepositional complements.

topics.headline: loudness includes overt publicity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden manner is public, overt loudness, not just a high decibel count.
topics.reason: The root field of loud/overt public manifestation fits the local speech setting and is not contradicted by the Form I surface.

topics.headline: second verb completes the paired restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two axes of excess: raising above and loud public address.
topics.reason: The second verb is coordinated with the first and later echoed by the verbal noun from the same root.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus third-person masculine suffix, locally directing the loud address toward the Prophet
words.prose: {{ar:لَهُۥ}} ({{tr:lahu}}) directs the loud address to him, with the suffix resuming the nearby Prophet title. The lām here is directional rather than a loose benefit marker: the prohibited loudness is aimed at the Prophet. Its contrast with the later peer-recipient phrase makes the difference between prophetic address and ordinary mutual address visible.

topics.headline: suffix routes loud speech to the Prophet
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second prohibition is about how speech is directed to the Prophet, not merely about loudness in general.
topics.reason: Attachment and cross-reference evidence make the suffix the governed complement of the loudness verb and identify its antecedent as the Prophet title.

topics.headline: him contrasts with peer recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that speech toward the Prophet is contrasted with ordinary peer-to-peer address.
topics.reason: The later comparison phrase supplies the peer target, while this pronoun marks the Prophet-directed target.

words.gloss_range: proclitic preposition marking the speech medium or specification after the loudness verb
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches the speech noun as the medium or specification of the loudness. It keeps the command focused on loudness in speech, and its tight proclitic form begins the chain of adjuncts that define target, medium, and comparison after the verb.

topics.headline: preposition marks the speech medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the loudness is specified as loudness with speech, not an unspecified noise.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following speech noun the governed complement of this preposition with the loudness verb.

words.gloss_range: definite verbal noun for speech as a class or domain, locally the medium of loud address
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speech, utterance, statement, and discourse; locally narrowed to speech as the medium of loud address
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْقَوْلِ}} ({{tr:al-qawli}}) names speech as a definite domain, so the prohibition reaches the act of saying itself, not only emotional tone. The {{ar:ق و ل}} ({{tr:q-w-l}}) range includes saying, utterance, opinion, and discourse, but the local gerund with the preposition narrows it to speech as the medium of loud address. Its placement mediates between the loudness verb and the peer-loudness model.

topics.headline: definite gerund covers speech as class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command regulates the speech act as a domain, not just a single quoted statement.
topics.reason: QAC marks a definite gerund governed by the preposition attached to the loudness verb.

topics.headline: discourse range narrowed to loud speech medium
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that loudness is attached to the speech-domain itself, while broader opinion or discourse senses remain background only.
topics.reason: The local prepositional complement selects speech-medium, and the loudness pairing supports the speech-loudness relation without activating every root branch.

words.gloss_range: comparison particle introducing the peer-loudness model that the Prophet-directed speech must not resemble
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) introduces the comparison that defines the forbidden manner. The command does not leave loudness abstract; it says the Prophet-directed speech must not resemble ordinary peer loudness. The compact proclitic form fuses the comparison to the loudness noun and pivots the reader from target to social register.

topics.headline: comparison supplies the forbidden model
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the problem is treating the Prophet-directed address like ordinary mutual address.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the comparison phrase a complement of the loudness verb, and the ellipsis guardrail confirms the compressed compared speech manner.

words.gloss_range: construct verbal noun of loudness after the comparison particle, locally nominalizing the prohibited loud act
words.root_gloss_range: loudness, openness, and public manifestation; locally narrowed to the nominal model of peer loudness
words.prose: {{ar:جَهْرِ}} ({{tr:jahri}}) turns the earlier loudness action into a noun inside the comparison. As a construct after the comparison particle, it binds the model of loudness to the peer term that follows. The {{ar:ج ه ر}} ({{tr:j-h-r}}) field of public openness remains visible: what is forbidden is not simply speech volume, but importing open peer-style loudness into address to the Prophet.

topics.headline: verbal noun models the loud action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison names a social manner of loudness rather than repeating the verb mechanically.
topics.reason: QAC marks a genitive gerund in construct after the comparison particle, with the following peer term as its complement.

topics.headline: loudness root repeats inside the prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same loudness root moving from verb to noun, making the second prohibition echo within itself.
topics.reason: The local verb and gerund share the same root and are connected by the comparison construction.

words.gloss_range: possessed part-word beginning the reciprocal peer construction inside the comparison
words.root_gloss_range: part, portion, mutual one-another constructions, with a cut-part image in the background; locally a community-internal peer term
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْضِكُمْ}} ({{tr:baʿḍikum}}) begins the peer model as a possessed part-word: some of you addressing others of you. The suffix keeps the model inside the believer community, and the {{ar:ب ع ض}} ({{tr:b-ʿ-ḍ}}) part/portion range helps the comparison feel like ordinary intra-group exchange rather than prophetic address. The same reciprocal social pattern also resonates with the surah’s later speech-ethics warning in 49:12.

topics.headline: possessed part-word marks internal peers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden comparison is ordinary internal peer-to-peer loudness among the addressees.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word the genitive complement of the loudness noun, and the suffix ties it to the addressed group.

topics.headline: part-image supports reciprocal social template
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the community split into reciprocal parts, a template later important for communal speech ethics (49:12).
topics.reason: The local construction selects the standard one-another function; the cut-part image remains supportive background, not a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: directional lām marking the second peer term as recipient within the reciprocal model
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks the second peer term as recipient inside the reciprocal comparison. It parallels the earlier lām attached to him but changes the target: not prophetic recipient, but peer recipient. That small preposition helps the comparison move from address to the Prophet into ordinary one-another speech.

topics.headline: lām directs loudness to a peer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison has a recipient structure: some of you loudly to others.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following peer noun the prepositional complement of this lām.

topics.headline: target shifts from him to one another
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the target contrast between speech to the Prophet and speech to peers.
topics.reason: The earlier pronoun complement and this later peer complement create the lām reprise noted in the critical rows.

words.gloss_range: indefinite part-word completing the generalized peer-to-peer comparison
words.root_gloss_range: part, portion, and one-another constructions; locally the indefinite peer recipient in a reciprocal frame
words.prose: {{ar:بَعْضٍ}} ({{tr:baʿḍin}}) completes the reciprocal model as an indefinite peer recipient. Without the suffix of the first peer term, it generalizes the comparison: not one named subgroup, but the ordinary way one part of the community addresses another. The {{ar:ب ع ض}} ({{tr:b-ʿ-ḍ}}) range is therefore narrowed to the one-another construction while retaining the sense of social parts facing each other.

topics.headline: indefinite peer completes the model
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the peer-loudness model is generalized rather than attached to one named party.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word the complement of the directional lām within the comparison phrase.

topics.headline: part-word formula narrowed to local mutuality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a compact one-another template: some of you to some others.
topics.reason: The local phrase selects reciprocal peer reference; broader part imagery remains supportive, not a separate activated branch.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle introducing the feared or cautionary consequence clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) opens the consequence clause and compresses the warning. It governs the subjunctive verb that follows, so the loss of deeds is not a detached afterthought but the feared outcome attached to the prohibited speech posture. Because one clause gathers the warning after both prohibitions, the risk covers the whole pattern of voice excess and peer-style loudness, with 49:3 supplying the lowered-voice counterpart.

topics.headline: particle introduces feared consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deed-loss warning is grammatically bound to the speech prohibitions.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the following clause as the cautioned outcome of the loudness prohibition, with the particle governing the subjunctive verb.

topics.headline: single warning gathers both restraints
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one compressed warning clause makes the whole forbidden speech posture dangerous, not only the nearest word.
topics.reason: The clause follows the coordinated prohibitions and the critical rows license broad scope over the warned speech posture.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form I verb of deeds becoming void; locally intransitive collapse rather than named external destruction
words.root_gloss_range: becoming void, failing, and the visceral collapse or bloating image; locally the nullification of deeds from within
words.prose: {{ar:تَحْبَطَ}} ({{tr:taḥbaṭa}}) makes the consequence severe: deeds may become void from within, without naming an external destroyer. Its feminine singular subjunctive agrees with the broken-plural deeds, and the {{ar:ح ب ط}} ({{tr:ḥ-b-ṭ}}) field of collapse or bloating gives the nullification a visceral image. The fixed deed-nullification pairing is active here, but the local trigger is speech-manner failure; the variant result-link reading is useful contrast, while the main reading keeps the warning under the preceding particle. The consequence also mirrors the surah’s later warning structure of regret after action (49:6).

topics.headline: verb agrees with deeds in the warning clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warned loss is grammatically attached to the deeds that follow.
topics.reason: QAC marks a subjunctive imperfect verb whose feminine singular agreement fits the following broken plural subject.

topics.headline: deeds become void from within
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a silent internal ruin of deeds rather than an externally narrated punishment.
topics.reason: The local Form I verb with deeds as subject supports intransitive nullification, while the root image supplies visceral pressure.

topics.headline: fixed deed-nullification formula enters speech ethics
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a severe Quranic deed-nullification formula is applied here to speech conduct.
topics.reason: The collocation rows tie this root to deeds across the corpus, and the local subject is the addressees’ deeds.

topics.headline: variant linkage and consequence mirror kept as contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural landing from commands into loss, with a variant result-link and the 49:6 consequence pattern sharpening the warning without replacing the main parse.
topics.reason: The main reading keeps the verb governed by the preceding particle; the variant and 49:6 parallel are retained as apparatus and structural contrast.

words.gloss_range: possessed broken plural deed-noun as grammatical subject of the voiding verb
words.root_gloss_range: work, action, and sustained intentional effort; locally accumulated deeds or works personally attached to the addressees
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ}} ({{tr:aʿmālukum}}) is not the object of a named destroyer; it is the grammatical subject of the voiding verb. That syntax moves focus from believers as actors to their personally possessed works as the vulnerable site of loss. The {{ar:ع م ل}} ({{tr:ʿ-m-l}}) range points to intentional, sustained effort, and the broken plural with the suffix makes a whole accumulated field of deeds personally at risk. The same deeds-root later helps frame the surah’s faith-and-obedience tests (49:14; 49:18).

topics.headline: deeds are subject and affected site
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deeds themselves are where the loss appears, not a passive object after a named agent.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as the nominative subject of the voiding verb.

topics.headline: possessed plural makes the risk personal and cumulative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the risk attaches to the addressees’ own accumulated works, not to an abstract category.
topics.reason: QAC marks a broken plural noun with second-person possessive suffix, and the suffix echoes the addressee chain.

topics.headline: intentional work field links faith and consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is endangered is sustained intentional effort, tied to the surah’s faith-and-works frame (49:14; 49:18).
topics.reason: The root range and cooccurrence rows support intentional work and faith-deeds linkage, while local grammar keeps the word as the plural deed subject.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial conjunction introducing the simultaneous unaware state
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is circumstantial, not simple coordination. It binds the final clause as the state accompanying deed-loss: the loss and the lack of perception are simultaneous. The clause may attach most closely to the consequence or cover the broader prohibited speech posture, and in either case it answers the divine hearing and knowledge frame of 49:1 with human imperception.

topics.headline: circumstantial conjunction makes loss simultaneous
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that non-perception is concurrent with the threatened loss, not a later separate event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the final clause as circumstantial, accompanying the deed-voiding verb.

topics.headline: unaware state covers the speech posture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between God’s hearing and knowledge in 49:1 and human non-perception at the end of 49:2.
topics.reason: The circumstantial clause is syntactically tied to the consequence and can semantically cover the prohibited speech posture.

words.gloss_range: independent second-person plural pronoun explicitly naming the addressees in the circumstantial clause
words.prose: {{ar:أَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:antum}}) makes the subject of imperception explicit even though the following verb already carries second-person plural agreement. The pronoun isolates the addressees themselves: you yourselves may be unaware while the loss is occurring. Its sound also binds the closing clause to the final verb, keeping personal responsibility audible to the end.

topics.headline: explicit pronoun personalizes imperception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing warning lands on the addressees themselves, not on an abstract lack of awareness.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this independent pronoun the subject of the circumstantial nominal clause, with the following verb as predicate.

topics.headline: pronoun sound binds to closing verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible binding between the explicit pronoun and the final perception verb.
topics.reason: The phonetic row is local to the pronoun and final verb and supports the clause’s closing effect.

words.gloss_range: factual negative particle before an indicative verb, contrasting with the earlier prohibitive particles
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is the same particle sound heard earlier, but its grammar has changed. Before the indicative perception verb, it states a fact of non-perception rather than issuing a prohibition. That shift makes the ayah descend from two commands that preserve agency into a closing condition where the addressees do not even register the loss.

topics.headline: third particle states non-perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause is not a command to perceive but a statement that perception is absent.
topics.reason: QAC and the following indicative verb distinguish this factual negative particle from the earlier prohibitive particles.

topics.headline: same sound shifts from command to fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the devastating pattern: do not, do not, then you do not perceive.
topics.reason: The three occurrences are visible in the local ayah sequence, with this final one selected by indicative grammar as factual negation.

words.gloss_range: indicative perception verb negated as a factual state, locally subtle awareness rather than command to perceive
words.root_gloss_range: sensing, subtle perception, sign-recognition, poetic discernment, and fine awareness; locally the failure to feel or register the loss
words.prose: {{ar:تَشْعُرُونَ}} ({{tr:tashʿurūna}}) closes the ayah as an indicative factual verb, agreeing with the explicit pronoun before it. The warning is not that they are commanded to perceive, but that they may lack subtle felt awareness while deeds are becoming void. The {{ar:ش ع ر}} ({{tr:sh-ʿ-r}}) field of sensing, sign-recognition, and fine perception makes the loss frighteningly quiet: it can fall below the threshold of feeling. The recurring formula of not perceiving marks unseen catastrophe elsewhere (2:9; 6:123; 16:26; 26:202), and the ayah’s frame is sharp because those named by faith at the opening can end in imperception.

topics.headline: indicative verb confirms factual negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing verb states an actual lack of perception and resumes the named addressees.
topics.reason: QAC marks an indicative second-person plural verb, and attachment evidence makes it the predicate of the explicit pronoun.

topics.headline: subtle awareness field makes the loss quiet
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the absent faculty is fine felt perception, not simply abstract knowledge.
topics.reason: The local verb selects perception; broader hair, poetry, and sign-family associations are retained only to sharpen the subtle-awareness field.

topics.headline: formula marks loss beneath awareness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word joins a recurring formula for catastrophe arriving below awareness (2:9; 6:123; 16:26; 26:202).
topics.reason: The critical rows provide concrete formula references and the local consequence is deed-loss beneath perception.

topics.headline: sound texture closes on constrained perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final sound texture reinforces the constricted, missed awareness at the ayah’s close.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows are local to the closing verb and fit the root’s perception field without altering grammar.

activation_trace.role: The branch contributes vocal highness and makes acoustic elevation the mechanism's literal input.
Audible voicing supplies the medium in which the two parties are comparatively positioned.
Higher rank converts the spatial word 'above' into a live status relation rather than a decibel comparison alone.

changed_reading.before: Do not speak more loudly than the Prophet.
changed_reading.after: Do not use audible force to make your own voice function as the higher-ranking voice.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Words 5, 9, 11, and 13 join raising, the Prophet, open voicing, and speech.
baseline_models.mechanism: A speaker can elevate an utterance by publishing and circulating it. Doing so over the one who brings news from God competes for control of the public information channel.

activation_trace.role: Public announcement turns raising from sheer loudness into amplification and onward transmission.
The God-reporting messenger supplies the authorized source whose channel can be crowded out.
Open voicing supplies the act by which private speech is made publicly forceful.
Circulating talk supplies the propagation path through which a competing voice gains reach.

changed_reading.before: The problem is an impolite tone in the Prophet's presence.
changed_reading.after: The problem can also be channel capture: self-authored talk is amplified until it competes with transmitted prophetic news.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The simile at words 14-16 compares addressing the Prophet with the believers' ordinary loud address to one another.
baseline_models.mechanism: The forbidden comparison imports a horizontal peer protocol into a non-interchangeable relation. Mutual talk and negotiation become a leveling device when applied to the prophetic addressee.

activation_trace.role: Portions of one whole supply the ordinary interchangeable peer relation expressed by 'one another.'
Mutual verbal negotiation supplies the familiar reciprocal register improperly transferred to this address.
The prophetic reporting function blocks reduction of the addressee to one ordinary social portion among others.

changed_reading.before: Use a more polite version of normal conversation with the Prophet.
changed_reading.after: Do not flatten a message-bearing relation into ordinary peer exchange or bargaining.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The result clause at words 17-22 connects the speech prohibition to the collapse of works without felt awareness.
baseline_models.mechanism: The loss behaves like latent bodily or reservoir damage: harmful intake can create apparent fullness while producing collapse, and stored water can vanish. Vocal self-inflation can therefore consume accumulated intentional work before the speaker detects it.

activation_trace.role: Swelling caused by harmful grazing supplies a material pattern of impressive expansion that is actually destructive.
Disappearing well water supplies the image of an accumulated reserve silently draining away.
Intentional work identifies what the speech event silently depletes.
Subtle awareness supplies the missing faculty, explaining why the damage need not register as an event.

changed_reading.before: A breach may cancel good deeds as a later penalty.
changed_reading.after: Self-amplifying speech may itself be a latent damage process that puffs up the speaker while draining the stored value of intentional work.

context_deltas.mechanism: The prior ayah converts acoustic elevation into procedural precedence. Raising one's voice can mean presenting one's position into the authoritative slot before the divine-messenger sequence has spoken.

activation_trace.role: Presenting something before an authority lets vocal raising operate as advancing a case, not only increasing volume.
Forward movement and precedence supply the temporal ordering that revises the focus prohibition.
Position before the hands locates the premature presentation in the immediate field of authority.
Messenger and message identify the authorized communication sequence that must not be preempted.

structural_cues: 49:1 and 49:2 repeat the same address and prohibition while shifting from going ahead to being above.
Temporal precedence in 49:1 and vertical precedence in 49:2 form two coordinates of the same displacement.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent prohibitions against going ahead and going above; I infer that vocal elevation can seize an earlier decision slot. A live alternative is that the two prohibitions are parallel manners without a shared procedure.

changed_reading.before: Do not outrank the Prophet acoustically.
changed_reading.after: Do not advance your own presentation so that it arrives as the operative judgment before the authorized message.

context_deltas.mechanism: Lowering the voice is coupled to testing and refining the inner core for protective restraint. Acoustic reduction becomes an assay that reveals and forms which authority the heart will let govern it.

activation_trace.role: Audible sound is the outward variable deliberately reduced in the contextual sequence.
Holding back by lowering and diminishing supplies the active operation performed on the voice.
A test that exposes what is in the heart makes vocal restraint diagnostically revealing.
Refining after examination makes the same restraint formative rather than merely evidentiary.
The pure core of a thing identifies the interior being exposed and refined.
Placing the self within protection supplies the inward capacity produced or disclosed by the assay.

structural_cues: 49:3 orders lowered voices, tested hearts, protective restraint, covering, and reward in one consequence chain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies vocal reduction followed by heart-testing and protection; I infer a diagnostic and formative arrow from restraint to the exposed core. A live alternative is that the lowered voice merely identifies people whose hearts were already refined.

changed_reading.before: Voice control is an external etiquette protecting works from penalty.
changed_reading.after: Voice control is an inward assay: the ability to reduce one's acoustic rank reveals and refines a heart capable of protective restraint.

context_deltas.mechanism: The loud call travels across an enclosing boundary and tries to pull the addressee into the caller's timetable. Waiting lets disclosure and emergence remain controlled from inside the protected space.

activation_trace.role: The surprise-raid branch gives open voicing an invasive temporal edge when it arrives without permission.
A voice's reach across distance supplies the means by which the caller crosses space without entering it.
Concealment behind a back supplies the protected inside whose availability the call tries to override.
Prevention and enclosure make the chamber a functional boundary rather than incidental scenery.
Holding the self back supplies the alternative to forcing access by vocal projection.
Movement from inside to outside identifies the event whose timing should remain with the addressee.

structural_cues: 49:4 places callers outside and the Prophet behind chambers; 49:5 contrasts calling with waiting for his emergence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distant calling, enclosure, waiting, and emergence; I infer that loudness attempts to command access and time. A live alternative is that these ayat regulate one physical episode without extending the boundary mechanism back into 49:2.

changed_reading.before: Do not address the Prophet at excessive volume.
changed_reading.after: Do not use vocal reach to breach protected availability or force the Prophet to appear on the speaker's timetable.

context_deltas.mechanism: A report can move from arrival to public salience to targeted action. When loudness substitutes for clarification, an unverified voice acquires operative force, strikes a group, and leaves regret after the damage is no longer reversible.

activation_trace.role: Broadcasting a report supplies the amplification stage that can grant a claim public force.
Reporting from God identifies the protected source against which other reports must not win by volume.
Incoming reported news supplies the informational object that can be amplified or examined.
Disclosure and clarification supply the missing checkpoint between report and action.
Aimed impact on a target turns information-channel failure into concrete social injury.
Impulsive disturbance of forbearance explains how salience outruns verification.
Regret over what has passed supplies delayed awareness after the actionable mistake.

structural_cues: 49:6 explicitly sequences report, clarification, impact on a people, action, and regret.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies that report-to-impact sequence; I infer that raising a voice over the prophetic channel can let salience bypass verification. A live alternative is that 49:6 concerns only unreliable messengers, while 49:2 concerns decorum around a reliable one.

changed_reading.before: A competing voice is disrespectful because it is too prominent.
changed_reading.after: A competing voice is dangerous because prominence can masquerade as evidentiary authority and route an unverified report into harmful action.

context_deltas.mechanism: Vocal superiority can be a pressure signal intended to make the Messenger follow the group's preferred commands. The focus prohibition protects the direction of guidance from inversion, because compliance in the wrong direction produces hardship.

activation_trace.role: Overpowering superiority supplies the coercive force implicit in placing one's voice above another.
Arrogating judgment over another supplies the governance claim carried by the forceful address.
The Messenger's message-bearing office fixes the proper direction of guidance.
Compliance supplies the relation that the group's pressure would reverse.
Demand and obligation identify the many matters in which the group would make its preference binding.
Severe difficulty supplies the system-level consequence of reversed compliance.

structural_cues: 49:7 places the Messenger among the audience, then imagines him obeying them in many matters and names the resulting hardship.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a hypothetical Messenger-to-group obedience path and its harmful result; I infer that raised address is one pressure mechanism seeking that inversion. A live alternative is that the obedience hypothetical diagnoses bad preferences without describing the function of loud speech.

changed_reading.before: The believers must sound deferential to the Prophet.
changed_reading.after: The believers must not use vocal force to reverse the guidance loop and turn the Messenger into an executor of their preferences.

context_deltas.mechanism: Acoustic out-ranking is readable as a low-amplitude form of exceeding one's limit. Left socially uncorrected, the same superiority logic partitions peers into opposed parties; repair removes estrangement and restores the binding relation.

activation_trace.role: Overpowering superiority supplies the small-scale dominance pattern carried by a voice placed above another.
Portioning supplies the latent possibility that 'one another' becomes separated parts rather than a coordinated whole.
Crossing the limit through aggression supplies the expanded social form of superiority.
Mutual combat supplies the terminal opposed-party state of an unrestrained dominance loop.
Removing mutual estrangement supplies the reversal that reopens coordination between parties.
A binding tie supplies the social structure that repair is meant to preserve.

structural_cues: The focus's 'one another' is followed later by two fighting parties and then by the declaration of brotherhood.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies acoustic superiority, later limit-crossing, factional combat, repair, and binding; I infer a scale-continuous dominance mechanism. A live alternative is that the conflict ayat change domains and do not imply escalation from vocal conduct.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition protects a singular sacred encounter.
changed_reading.after: It also interrupts a portable dominance habit at its vocal scale before that habit partitions the community and requires coercive repair.

context_deltas.mechanism: Ordinary speech among peers can wound a shared social self. Faulting another is framed as faulting oneself, and absent-person speech becomes consumption of kinship flesh; this gives the focus's work-loss a communal feedback path rather than a private penalty only.

activation_trace.role: Parts of one whole let reciprocal speakers remain members of a shared body even while addressing one another.
Damage from harmful intake supplies the feedback by which corrosive speech returns against the speaker's works.
Verbal faulting supplies the immediate act that injures another through speech.
The very self or identity makes another member's verbal injury reflexive self-injury.
Mentioning a person in absence supplies the speech practice converted into bodily consumption.
Corruption and tale-bearing between people directly links verbal circulation with destructive consumption.
Kinship tissue supplies the social body being consumed by hostile peer speech.
Brotherhood makes the consumed body relationally continuous with the speaker.

structural_cues: 49:11 words 27-28 add reciprocal name-calling and labels; their roots are branchless in the packet and are used here only as structural evidence.
49:12 repeats 'some of you, others' and immediately renders backbiting as eating a dead brother's flesh.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies self-directed grammar, absent-person speech, eating, kinship tissue, and brotherhood; I infer a communal-body feedback arrow into the focus's work-loss. A live alternative is that later peer prohibitions are separate wrongs and do not explain the focus consequence.

changed_reading.before: The peer register is harmless elsewhere but inappropriate with the Prophet.
changed_reading.after: The comparison to peer speech is diagnostic, not an endorsement: ordinary verbal habits can consume the shared social self, and importing them upward exposes the speaker's own works to the same damage.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context does not erase distinctions but changes their purpose and metric. Social branching serves recognition, while honor is measured by protective restraint; vocal prominence and reputation therefore cannot manufacture true rank.

activation_trace.role: High status supplies the rank claim that vocal raising can perform.
Good repute supplies the reputational reward a prominent voice may seek.
Branching and differentiation supply real social plurality without making loudness its hierarchy.
Recognition through a distinguishing trace gives social difference an epistemic purpose.
Commendable honor supplies the genuine rank whose criterion the ayah relocates.
Self-protection supplies the inward metric of honor in place of acoustic or reputational dominance.

structural_cues: 49:13 moves from created differences to mutual recognition and then explicitly identifies the criterion of honor.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies social differentiation, recognition, honor, and protective restraint; I infer that 49:2 rejects voice as a counterfeit rank technology. A live alternative is that 49:13 corrects lineage hierarchy only, without revising acoustic hierarchy.

changed_reading.before: Do not audibly claim a rank above the Prophet.
changed_reading.after: Do not use volume or public repute to manufacture rank; difference is for recognition, and honor is relocated to self-protective restraint.

context_deltas.mechanism: An uttered identity claim can be louder than the state it names. The sequence contrasts saying with inward entry, tests truth through costly action, and rejects informing God about one's religion; vocal prominence becomes self-certification without corresponding interior or enacted evidence.

activation_trace.role: Trusting inward assent supplies the state that a verbal identity claim cannot create by assertion.
Saying what is not or falsely attributing it supplies the risk of vocal self-certification.
Overt utterance supplies the repeated surface claim that is corrected and renamed.
Interior and hidden state supply the domain into which faith has not yet passed.
The inner core supplies the locus whose condition can diverge from public speech.
Expenditure of capacity under hardship supplies enacted evidence that a voiced claim lacks by itself.
Fulfilling a claim through action supplies the truth criterion beyond verbal force.
Knowledge as disclosed reality blocks the speaker from making self-report the source of divine knowledge.
Obedient submission supplies the lived relation that cannot be established by loudly teaching its label.

structural_cues: 49:14 explicitly contrasts 'we believe' with 'say we submit' and faith's not-yet entry into hearts.
49:14 word 20 supplies an explicit non-diminution contrast for works; its root is branchless in the packet and is used only structurally.
49:15 moves from profession to doubtlessness, costly action, and truth, while 49:16 rejects teaching God one's religion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies corrected speech, inward entry, enacted truth, and complete divine knowledge; I infer that vocal elevation can function as unsupported self-certification. A live alternative is that these ayat distinguish stages of affiliation without commenting on vocal authority.

changed_reading.before: Believers should lower the delivery of otherwise valid speech.
changed_reading.after: A forceful religious claim may outrun the inward and enacted reality it names, so the ayah also restrains self-certifying speech.

context_deltas.mechanism: A raised religious voice can position the speaker as creditor, burdening the addressee with a reminder of the speaker's supposed favor. The context reverses the vector: gentle guidance toward faith is the favor received, not a contribution for which the Messenger owes recognition.

activation_trace.role: Elevation of rank supplies the creditor-like posture enacted by the raised voice.
Arrogating judgment over another supplies the entitlement implicit in demanding recognition.
Burdening a beneficiary by rehearsing a favor identifies the speech-act whose direction is corrected.
Gentle indication toward the true path supplies the actual benefit flowing toward the believers.
Truth verified in fulfillment keeps the claimed religious status answerable to reality.

structural_cues: 49:17 repeats the favor-claim three times and explicitly reverses who confers the benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a spoken favor-claim and an explicit reversal toward divine guidance; I infer that raised speech can perform creditor status. A live alternative is that boasting about submission is a distinct vice unrelated to the focus's comparative voice.

changed_reading.before: Loud address elevates the speaker over the Messenger in the moment.
changed_reading.after: Loud religious address can also elevate the speaker into an imagined creditor who expects the Messenger to acknowledge a favor, although guidance flowed the other way.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's lack of awareness is perspectival, not evidentiary absence. Work-loss may disappear below the actor's perception while remaining fully visible to an observer whose sight includes both hidden conditions and performed deeds.

activation_trace.role: Vanishing well water supplies a reserve loss that can occur beneath ordinary surface monitoring.
Subtle awareness names the actor-side sensor that fails to register the depletion.
What is concealed from eyes supplies the hidden layer in which loss can escape self-observation.
Complete seeing supplies an observer perspective that does not share the actor's blind spot.
Intentional deeds are the common object linking the hidden loss in the focus with final observation.

structural_cues: The surah closes by joining knowledge of the unseen with sight of what the audience does.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies hiddenness, complete sight, and performed work; I infer an observer asymmetry that explains 'while you do not perceive.' A live alternative is that 49:18 gives a general assurance of omniscience without specifying the mechanics of work-loss in 49:2.

changed_reading.before: The speaker receives no warning that works have been lost.
changed_reading.after: The speaker's missing feedback is itself part of the danger: depletion can be hidden from the actor while remaining fully seen in the evaluation of deeds.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates an ocular branch of the focus root for open voicing. It remains anchored in the repeated focus root and directly explains the focus's absent awareness; downstream prose should present it as a material analogy, not as the lexical gloss of the verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus repeats open voicing at words 11 and 14, then ends with failure to perceive at word 22.

activation_trace.role: An eye overwhelmed by sunlight supplies the paradox that excessive manifestation can disable perception.
Subtle awareness supplies the perceptual capacity lost under the glare of self-display.
Insight of the heart supplies the intact perception contrasted with the speaker's self-dazzling.

changed_reading.before: The speaker simply fails to notice an externally imposed consequence.
changed_reading.after: The act of making oneself maximally manifest may generate its own glare, so vocal self-display helps blind the speaker to the loss it causes.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it combines the arrow-nock branch of 'above' with the stray-shot branch supplied under the Prophet's root. Both are focus-anchored and 49:6 supplies targeted impact; downstream prose should mark this as a transmission analogy, never as a translation of the focus words.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The sequence 'voices above the Prophet's voice' at words 6-9 is followed by the danger of work-loss.

activation_trace.role: The notch where a bowstring sits turns 'above' into a supplied image of fitting something for release.
A shot that swerves supplies the risk that a report-like projectile departs from its proper line.
Broadcasting supplies the launch from speaker into public circulation.
Aimed impact on a target supplies the social endpoint of the launched report.

changed_reading.before: A raised voice merely occupies more acoustic space.
changed_reading.after: A voice elevated over the prophetic channel can behave like a nocked report: fitted for public release, liable to swerve, and capable of striking a social target.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it joins the tiny biting-pest branch of 'some' to harmful grazing and social consumption. The chain remains anchored in the focus's repeated 'one another' and collapse clause, with 49:12 supplying a material speech analogy; downstream prose should qualify it as a scale-and-metabolism model rather than word substitution.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Words 15-19 move directly from reciprocal portions to the collapse of works.

activation_trace.role: A tiny biting pest supplies the scale mismatch by which a small verbal act can carry disproportionate harm.
Harmful grazing supplies the ingestion process that produces swelling and ruin rather than nourishment.
Consumption as decay and irritation supplies the continuing corrosive action of the verbal bite.
Kinship tissue identifies the communal substance on which the corrosive speech feeds.

changed_reading.before: Only conspicuously loud disrespect threatens works.
changed_reading.after: Even a socially tiny verbal bite can enter a harmful consumption cycle, swell the speaking self, corrode kinship tissue, and quietly ruin works.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This activation uses the packet's non-dominant mapped root for the focus's speech root, so it is deliberately form-distant. It remains valid as a supplied split-root contrast with settled faith and later doubt; downstream prose should call it an acoustic-psychological analogy and preserve its uncertainty.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus addresses believers at word 3 and regulates their speech at word 13, allowing a contrast between inward settlement and outward verbal motion.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant split branch contributes rattling instability, recasting forceful saying as oscillation rather than settled authority.
Settled security supplies the inward stability against which the rattling surface voice is tested.
Oscillating doubt supplies a contextual psychological analogue for unstable verbal insistence.

changed_reading.before: A loud religious claim projects certainty and strength.
changed_reading.after: Its very insistence may be surface rattling around an unsettled center, the acoustic opposite of the secure assent invoked at the ayah's opening.

strongest_changes: Acoustic elevation became procedural preemption: a voice can occupy the judgment slot before the authorized message.
Lowering the voice became a heart assay that both reveals and refines protective restraint.
Public salience became an epistemic routing hazard capable of moving an unverified report into targeted harm.
Raised address became a control-loop inversion and later a self-certifying or creditor-like religious claim.
Unnoticed work-loss became a latent depletion process hidden from the actor but fully visible in the evaluation of deeds.
summary.what_was_special: The focus supports several coexisting mechanisms rather than one etiquette rule: rank production, channel capture, peer flattening, boundary and timing control, report-to-action routing, communal self-consumption, and latent work depletion. Material branches also preserved live outliers in which publicity dazzles, reports are launched, tiny speech bites poison the social body, and a forceful claim rattles around an unsettled center.
remaining_uncertainties: The grammar warns of work-collapse but does not by itself settle whether every mechanism is direct causation, exposed disposition, or threatened consequence.
The boundary, factional, and communal-body readings depend on carrying later social structures back into the focus rather than treating each ayah as a separate rule.
The projectile, grazing, dazzling, and non-dominant split-root readings are deliberately analogical and should not displace the stronger acoustic, procedural, and epistemic readings.
The context leaves open whether vocal restraint primarily forms the heart or reveals a heart already formed.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Volume can perform rank.** ر ف ع B010 ("highness of voice"), ف و ق B003 ("overpowering superiority"), and ص و ت B002 ("good repute") turn the doubled comparison of voices into a status mechanism. The packet supplies elevation, above-ness, and voiced reputation; I infer that louder speech can socially install the speaker above the prophet. The ayah prohibits an acoustic claim to precedence, not decibels alone.
2. **Inflated speech can produce an unseen internal collapse.** ح ب ط B001 ("belly swelling from harmful grazing") supplies the material image of deceptive enlargement, while ع م ل B007 ("self-exertion or taking trouble") names what is lost. The sequence loud expansion -> *habat* of works is explicit, but the physiological analogy is supplied by the branch; I infer that apparent enlargement consumes the value of accumulated exertion. The warning reads as anti-inflation: outward magnitude can conceal inward ruin.
3. **The danger lies beneath ordinary awareness.** ش ع ر B005 ("subtle knowing and awareness") is the direct verbal scope; B004 ("an inner garment touching the body") adds an exploratory proximity image. The ayah itself supplies "while you do not perceive" after social speech and lost works. I infer that the causal damage occurs as close to the agent as an inner garment yet below conscious notice. The close makes self-monitoring of speech structurally necessary.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The mockery, fault-finding, and backbiting of 49:11-12 showed that voice can injure rank, identity, and connective tissue even without literal loudness. Finally, 49:18's seeing of works corrected any purely acoustic reading: the threatened loss belongs to an interior field fully seen even when the speakers do not perceive it.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Vocal height performs a claim of rank and control.** `ر ف ع:B010` is specifically highness of voice, and `ص و ت:B001` supplies audible voicing; but `ف و ق:B002` and `ف و ق:B003` add higher rank and overpowering superiority. The contrast with “do not advance” in 49:1 and the deliberate lowering in 49:3 makes the vertical vocabulary social as well as acoustic. The packet supplies loudness and ranked above-ness; I infer that placing one voice over another enacts a bid to control whose word governs. The verse therefore prohibits not only noise but a vocalized seizure of precedence over prophetic informing (`ن ب ء:B003`).

2. **A voice can enlarge its public footprint while emptying the worth of action.** `ص و ت:B002` carries good public repute, `ج ه ر:B001` open declaration, and `ر ف ع:B005` the spreading of a report. These dormant public-circulation branches are activated by the report that arrives in 49:6 and by the repeated calling in 49:4. Against them, `ح ب ط:B001` images livestock swelling from harmful grazing until near death, while `ح ب ط:B005` images a well whose water disappears. The packet gives public amplification followed by the loss of works; I infer the material analogy that inflated verbal presence can coexist with depleted moral substance. **تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَٰلُكُمْ** thus reads as concealed internal ruin beneath apparent communicative enlargement.

3. **The danger is precisely below ordinary perception.** `ش ع ر:B005` supplies subtle awareness and noticing, not mere possession of information. Its negation follows the threatened collapse of intentional deeds (`ع م ل:B001`), and 49:6 later answers ignorance with deliberate clarification. The packet gives an unnoticed consequence and a later verification procedure; I infer that restraint is preventive because the actor cannot reliably feel the moral damage while producing it. “While you do not perceive” therefore turns etiquette into an epistemic safeguard against self-invisible loss.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayat 49:14–17 reveal that an elevated voice need not be acoustically loud: `ر ف ع:B005` (announcing or spreading a report) and `ص و ت:B002` (public repute) fit the advertised claims “we believe” and “our submission is a favor.” The acoustic command retrospectively exposes status-amplifying speech more broadly.

baseline.text: Ey iman edenler! Seslerinizi Peygamber'in sesinden daha fazla yükseltmeyin ve onunla, birbirinizle yüksek sesle konuştuğunuz gibi konuşmayın; yoksa siz farkında olmadan işleriniz boşa gider.

findings.text: Sesin yüksekliği, yalnız desibel değil, konuşanın sözünü Peygamber'in sözü üzerinde yönetici ve üstün kılan bir statü iddiası olabilir.
Kamusal sesi ve itibarı şişiren açık konuşma, dışarıda büyürken amellerin iç değerini tüketebilir; görünür genişleme ahlaki boşalmayı gizleyebilir.
Zararın bedene değen iç giysi kadar yakın fakat bilincin altında gerçekleştiği imgesi, konuşmanın gizli etkisini anlatmak için önerilir; ancak bu bağ fazla dolaylıdır.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: Vertical Calibration of Voice and Standing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Social relation is made audible and spatial through controlled height: voices rise or lower, and persons are elevated by genuine standing rather than self-assertion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Acoustic altitude becomes a diagnostic of social rank, yet the surah reverses the expected ladder by locating durable elevation in restraint and protected character.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Received Standing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Standing is elevated by tested quality, prior good, and conferred distinction rather than by the claimant's own lift.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: elevation in rank `quranic:root_000582:B002/m01`; height or loftiness `quranic:root_000745:B001/m01`; superior rank `quranic:root_001188:B002/m01`; granted distinction `quranic:root_001163:B002/m01`; inherent honor `quranic:root_001294:B001/m01`; greatness `quranic:root_001029:B001/m01`; public honor and inviolability `quranic:root_001029:B010/m01`; prior standing in good `quranic:root_001207:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: elevation and "above" occur at 49:2-3; greatness and reward at 49:3; distinction at 49:8; the name/height root at 49:11, 16, and 18; honor at 49:13; precedence at 49:1.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Rank language extends the voice scale into a social hierarchy, but its stable forms are received or recognized: tested quality, prior good, granted distinction, and protected honor. The scale is real, yet persons do not establish their own position merely by speaking from above.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Reliable knowledge requires controlled passage from arrival or concealment to disclosure, examination, and accountable judgment.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Epistemic discipline is materialized as target practice, unmarked terrain, tactile probing, a dawn raid, and the cleaning of a well until what it holds becomes visible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Unmarked Ground and Agitated Motion
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A traveler without landmarks loses orientation, becomes agitated, and moves before a route has been established.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: impulsive disturbance opposed to composure `quranic:root_000271:B002/m01`; unknown terrain without mark or prior use `quranic:root_000271:B003/m01`; agitation after stillness `quranic:root_000271:B005/m01`; road marker and appointed sign `quranic:root_000051:B005/m01`; traversing land without knowledge `quranic:root_000269:B009/m01`; landmark for orientation `quranic:root_001040:B002/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: ignorance occurs at 49:6; command/marker at 49:7 and 9; the public-voice root at 49:2; knowing/marking at 49:1, 7, 8, 13, 16, and 18.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Ignorance is not inert emptiness here. It is an unmarked setting that provokes restless motion: the traveler has neither prior knowledge nor a sign by which to orient. The scene explains why clarification must precede action, because agitation on unknown ground amplifies error rather than resolving it.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Report Becomes a Dawn Raid
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An arriving report triggers a surprise approach at daybreak, turning unverified information into an attack on an unprepared group.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: dawn and first light `quranic:root_000839:B001/m01`; arrival in the morning `quranic:root_000839:B002/m01`; morning raid and distress call `quranic:root_000839:B004/m01`; coming upon people at dawn unawares `quranic:root_000269:B005/m01`; calamity striking its object `quranic:root_000889:B004/m01`.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: the morning/state root and the striking root occur at 49:6; the public-arrival root occurs at 49:2.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The latent scene supplies a concrete form for harming people in ignorance. News arrives, armed movement follows before full visibility, and an unsuspecting group receives the strike. Morning is therefore not a neutral time marker: it is the interval in which premature certainty becomes irreversible action.
